1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. API: application programming interface; SDK: software development kit

  • Thinking: adaptive and extended thinking, effort, fast mode, and what they cost
  • Prompt caching: what is cached, TTLs, minimums, prices and how to check a hit
  • Batch versus realtime: when each fits, and how batches work
  • Third-party platforms: Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry
  • API errors and retries: the status codes, rate limits, backoff and request IDs

2Thinking, Effort and Fast Mode

Running case

Tidewater's Costly Answers

  • The claims assistant answers hard coverage questions well, but the monthly bill is high and some answers are slow
  • Most requests are simple lookups; a few need real reasoning
  • The team wants to spend reasoning only where it pays
Control What it does Notes
Adaptive thinking The model decides how much to think, steered by effort The mode on current models; no thinking field needed
Extended thinking Old name A fixed reasoning budget (budget_tokens) Older manual mode; rejected with a 400 error on current models, so use adaptive thinking [Verify live]
Effort (output_config.effort) low, medium, high, xhigh, max: how thorough and how many tokens A behavioral signal, not a hard budget; lower effort = faster and cheaper for routine work
Fast mode (speed: "fast") Faster output (up to about 2.5 times) at premium pricing For latency-critical work on supported models

  • Thinking tokens are billed as output tokens and count toward max_tokens, even if the text is not shown. Thinking blocks carry a signature and the text is a summary, not the raw reasoning.
  • Higher effort raises quality, latency and cost; step down when evals show quality holds, step up when they do not (Module 8).
Exam tip

"Reduce cost and latency on simple requests" → lower effort (or a smaller model); "reasoning quality too low on hard cases" → higher effort or a stronger model, checked with evals.

3Prompt Caching

Caching lets the API reuse the processed prefix of a prompt across requests, which cuts cost and latency for repeated content such as a long system prompt, policy text or tool definitions.

Fact Detail
How Automatic caching (one top-level cache_control; the breakpoint moves forward) or explicit breakpoints on content blocks (up to 4)
What is cached The full prefix, in order: tools, then system, then messages. A change earlier in the prefix invalidates what follows
Lifetime 5 minutes by default (refreshed on each hit); 1 hour optionally at a higher write price
Price Cache write about 1.25x the base input price (5 minutes) or 2x (1 hour); cache read about 0.1x (even less on some models)
Minimum size A minimum prompt length applies (for example 512 tokens on current models); shorter prompts are not cached, with no error
Check it The response usage shows cache_creation_input_tokens and cache_read_input_tokens
  • Design rule: stable text first, volatile text last. A timestamp or user name at the top of the prompt breaks the cache on every call.
  • Caching pays off when the same prefix is reused several times within the lifetime; a one-off prompt only pays the write cost.
  • Cached input tokens are not counted against the input tokens per minute rate limit the way uncached ones are Beyond the guide.

[Verify live] Current documentation: minimums, multipliers (read 0.1x, 0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, 0.025x on Fable 5.1) and TTL options. As of 8 November 2026.

4Realtime Versus Batch

Realtime (Messages API) Message Batches API
Response Immediate (seconds) Asynchronous: most finish within about an hour, up to 24 hours, no latency guarantee
Price Standard 50% lower
Use for Chat, interactive tools, blocking steps Non-urgent bulk work: overnight reports, evaluations, bulk classification
Mechanics One call, one answer Create the batch, poll its status, read results by custom_id (a batch holds up to 100,000 requests or 256 MB; results stay available about 29 days)
Limits Tool loops possible in your code Each request is one model call: no tool round trip inside a request

Exam tip

Tens of thousands of archived records, results not needed for days, cost is the concern → Message Batches API. Parallel realtime calls do not lower the per-token price, and a smaller model chosen only for price ignores quality.

5Third-Party Platforms

Claude is also available through Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud (Claude models on Google Cloud), Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS. Why use them: your existing cloud contract, billing, identity (IAM) and data-residency controls.

Topic What to know
Model IDs Differ by platform (for example anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 on Bedrock; the Claude API ID on Google Cloud and Foundry)
Auth The cloud provider's identity (IAM roles, service accounts), not an Anthropic API key
SDKs The client SDKs have platform-specific clients with the same request shape
Features Availability can lag or differ (for example images as base64 only on Bedrock); check the platform page
Lifecycle Partner platforms set their own retirement dates
  • Choose a platform from the requirements (Module 1): existing cloud commitment, residency, IAM integration. Use the first-party API when you need the newest features first.

6API Errors and Retries

Status Meaning Action
400 invalid request Malformed request (bad parameter, unsupported combination) Fix the request; do not retry unchanged
401 / 403 Bad key / no permission Fix credentials or access
404 / 413 Not found / request too large Fix the path or reduce the request
429 rate limit Too many requests or tokens Back off, honor retry-after, reduce concurrency
500 / 504 / overloaded Server-side or transient Retry with exponential backoff
  • Rate limits are measured in requests per minute, input tokens per minute and output tokens per minute, with a token-bucket that refills continuously; sharp increases in traffic can trigger acceleration limits, so ramp up gradually.
  • The official SDKs retry transient errors twice by default with exponential backoff; tune the retry count and timeouts.
  • Always log the request-id; an error can also arrive inside a stream (Module 2).
Exam tip

4xx: fix the request. 429: back off and honor retry-after. 5xx or overloaded: retry with exponential backoff.

7Exam Q&A

S1Tidewater wants to re-tag 80,000 archived claim emails for a quarterly audit that is due in a week; cost is the main concern and nobody waits on individual results. What fits best?

  • APick the largest model for every email to be safe
  • BSend 80,000 realtime requests in parallel so the audit finishes sooner
  • CSubmit them through the Batches API and read results by custom_id
  • DStream each request to reduce the waiting time
Show the answer

Answer: C. Latency-tolerant bulk work at lower cost is what batches are for; parallel realtime calls do not cut the per-token price.

S2The assistant sends the same 40-page policy text with every question, and requests are slow and costly. What is the best change?

  • AIncrease max_tokens
  • BPut the question first and the policy last so that the policy can change
  • CCache the stable prefix (the policy) with cache_control and put the question last
  • DRemove the policy from the prompt
Show the answer

Answer: C. A stable prefix with a cache breakpoint is reused at a fraction of the cost and latency.

S3A developer put the current time in the first line of the system prompt, and the cache hit rate is zero. Why?

  • AThe cache lifetime is only one second, so nothing survives between calls
  • BThe cache only works for images
  • CThe prefix changes on every request, so nothing matches the cached prefix
  • DTimestamps are not allowed in prompts
Show the answer

Answer: C. Any change early in the prefix invalidates the cache; volatile text must come last.

S4How can a developer verify that a request used the cache?

  • ARead the HTTP status code
  • BThe API sends a notification email whenever a cache entry is used
  • CCompare response times by eye
  • DThe cache fields in usage show writes and reads
Show the answer

Answer: D. The usage fields report cache writes and reads.

S5A prompt marked for caching is shorter than the model's minimum cacheable length. What happens?

  • AIt is processed normally, without caching and without an error
  • BA 400 error is returned because the prompt is below the minimum length
  • CThe cache is created anyway
  • DThe request is rejected
Show the answer

Answer: A. Prompts below the minimum are not cached, silently.

S6A request returns HTTP 429 with a retry-after header. What should the client do?

  • ASwitch to a bigger model
  • BWait the indicated time, back off exponentially and lower concurrency
  • CRetry immediately in a tight loop, again and again, until the request finally goes through
  • DDrop the request permanently
Show the answer

Answer: B. A rate limit calls for waiting, backoff and fewer concurrent calls.

S7A request returns 400 because of an unsupported parameter combination. What is the right response?

  • AFix the request, since a 400 will not succeed unchanged
  • BRetry the same request with backoff
  • CWait one hour and then send the very same request again, unchanged
  • DContact billing
Show the answer

Answer: A. Client errors need a corrected request, not a retry.

S8A company already runs on a cloud provider and needs Claude under its existing IAM and billing. What should it consider?

  • AIt is not possible to use Claude outside the first-party API
  • BCopy the first-party API key into the cloud account
  • CClaude through that provider's platform, accepting its model IDs and feature differences
  • DUse the provider's own model names with the first-party endpoint and the cloud's credentials
Show the answer

Answer: C. Claude is offered through major clouds with the cloud's identity and billing; IDs and feature availability differ.

S9Simple lookups and hard coverage questions use the same high-effort setting, so costs are high. What is a sound improvement?

  • AUse fast mode for every request so that every answer arrives as quickly as possible
  • BDisable the system prompt
  • CUse lower effort (or a smaller model) for simple requests, verified with evals
  • DSet effort to max everywhere
Show the answer

Answer: C. Reasoning should be spent where it improves results, and evals confirm the quality holds.

S10A developer sets a fixed budget_tokens for thinking on a current model and gets a 400 error. What is the likely cause?

  • AThinking needs batch mode
  • Bbudget_tokens must be larger than max_tokens for the request to be accepted
  • CThe API key is wrong
  • DManual extended thinking is not accepted on current models; use adaptive thinking with effort
Show the answer

Answer: D. Current models use adaptive thinking; the manual budget mode is rejected.

S11Which TWO statements about prompt caching are correct? Select TWO.

  • ACaching removes the need for a system prompt
  • BCache reads cost less than normal input tokens
  • CStable content should come first and changing content last
  • DAny text can be placed first because caching ignores order
  • ECached prompts never expire
Show the answer

Answer: B, C. The prefix must match, and reads are priced well below normal input; entries expire after their lifetime.

S12Which TWO are appropriate for the Message Batches API? Select TWO.

  • AA blocking approval check
  • BA nightly evaluation run over a test set
  • CA step inside a live tool loop that needs the tool result at once
  • DA chat reply that an adjuster is waiting for
  • EA weekly bulk re-classification of archived claims
Show the answer

Answer: B, E. Batches suit non-urgent bulk jobs; anything a person or a loop waits on needs realtime.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Thinking Adaptive by default; manual budget_tokens mode Old name rejected on current models; billed as output tokens, counts toward max_tokens
Effort low · medium · high · xhigh · max; lower = cheaper and faster
Fast mode speed: "fast": faster output at premium price
Caching Stable prefix first; 5 min (or 1 h); write ~1.25x, read ~0.1x; minimum size; check usage cache fields; up to 4 breakpoints
Batch 50% cheaper; up to 24 h; custom_id; poll; no mid-request tool loop
Realtime vs batch Someone waits → realtime; can wait and cost matters → batch
Platforms Bedrock, Google Cloud, Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS: cloud IAM, different IDs and features
Errors 4xx fix the request; 429 back off and honor retry-after; 5xx/overloaded retry with exponential backoff; SDK retries twice by default; log request-id
